newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary parliament passes social security budget.
newsitem.headline: Hungary parliament passes social security budget.

text.p: The Hungarian parliament on Thursday passed the 1997 social security budget, made up of the health and pension funds.
The two funds, originally forecast by the finance ministry to break even next year, envisage 13 billion forints of deficit, due to lower than planned expected revenues, press reports said.

The pension fund is expected to close next year with a deficit of 9.6 billion forints on revenues of 615 billion forints. The plan is calculated on the basis of a 19.5 percent increase in pensions in 1997. @
The health fund is expected to be in the red with 3.8 billion forints on revenues of 521 billion forints.
The social security budget is one of the two major components of the general government budget, the other being the central state budget which parliament cpassed on Tuesday.
The planned deficit of the general government budget, including social security, is 392 billion forints or 4.9 percent of the GDP, up from the four percent target for 1996.
The rise is mainly due to changes, called technical by the government and most analysts, in the accounting of state debt. @
According to the government forecast, Hungary's GDP will be around 7,960 billion forints next year.
This year's social security deficit is expected to amount to over 60 billion forints and already stood at 62 billion in September.
This compares to a 17.8 billion forint defciit target set when the International Monetary Fund (IMF) granted a $381 million stand-by loan facility with a maturity of 23 months to Hungary in March. @
However IMF experts visiting Budapest this week found that Hungary had still met the global requirements of the stand-by loan agreement.
